races.name: Celebrating National Racehorse Week Maiden Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: St Just In Time
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's hold-up operator was third over 2m (13f) on similar Good ground in comparable company, so the trip and conditions are fine, but he needs the leader to stop — which a controlled Iwanttobreakfree is unlikely to do; 12 days since last run is straightforward and no headgear concern.

runners_data.name: Wait At The Gate
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (⚠) and style unclassified, so tactical positioning on debut here is genuinely uncertain; went well on Good ground in his only comparable start (4th), but a 42-day break and Bridgwater's blank 14-day record (0/0) offer little confidence, and he simply may not know what he's doing positionally in a hurdles race.

runners_data.name: Iwanttobreakfree
runners_data.note: The pace anchor of this race — Dan Skelton's 4-year-old has gone 2-3-2 in bumper/hurdle company, both hurdle runs on Good over this exact trip, and Harry Skelton will dictate from the front unchallenged; tongue tie noted (hg:t) and trainer is in form at 7/26 over 14 days, making this a serious contender in the dominant shape.

runners_data.name: Nightflyer
runners_data.note: Jonjo Jr steers a prominent-style runner who has a win to his name (1/16f/SOF) and two course-distance runs under his belt; a 77-day absence is the main flag, and his Going form on Good is moderate (0W0P from two tries), but if he travels smoothly off the pace he is the most likely to pounce on a tiring Iwanttobreakfree.

runners_data.name: Maria Mes
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's 5-year-old has placed twice on Good ground over similar distances and is a clean prominent rider, so the setup suits tactically; she has never won in four hurdle starts and has drifted back to 12th on soft, suggesting the Good ground here is a positive rather than a negative — but needs jump fluency to stay in contention.

runners_data.name: Morissette
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fader in finishes (⚠) and returning from 116 days off the track for a small yard (0/2 in 14 days); her only exposed form run is an 8th on Soft, making her deeply unexposed on Good — Bryan Carver will likely have to ride positively to overcome the fitness query, but the finishing tendency works against her in any competitive scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Iwanttobreakfree is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of six and, with no other horse likely to seriously contest for the lead, Harry Skelton can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, nursing the 4-year-old through the 2m2½f trip on good ground at Newton Abbot. Nightflyer and Maria Mes are both prominently-ridden types who will sit just off the pace and keep the gallop honest without turning it into a true test of stamina. St Just In Time and Morissette are hold-up horses who will need something to go wrong up front, while Wait At The Gate's running style is unclassified and unlikely to be a genuine pace threat. With one uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable, self-selected tempo on ground that suits, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-front profiles — horses in the first two or three who can travel into the race without expending energy and pounce at the last — rather than late closers who will need a collapse from the leader that nothing in this setup makes likely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iwanttobreakfree Controls Easily
scenarios.trigger: If Iwanttobreakfree bowls along uncontested and Skelton produces a controlled, measured display from the front.
scenarios.body: Skelton sets a fair but sustainable gallop, the prominent pair of Nightflyer and Maria Mes track without threatening, and Iwanttobreakfree finds more when pressed approaching the last to hold on; his good-ground form (two seconds from two tries on Good) and trainer's 7/26 in 14 days make this the form outcome.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Him Back
scenarios.trigger: If Nightflyer and Maria Mes apply enough relentless pressure to force a stronger gallop that drains Iwanttobreakfree's stamina reserves late.
scenarios.body: Both prominent runners sit tight throughout and pounce at the second-last when the leader begins to tie up; Nightflyer's previous course-distance win on similar ground gives him a meaningful profile edge here, and Jonjo Jr can time a late surge well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a finish for the hold-up horses and the leader fades inside the final flight.
scenarios.body: St Just In Time, third over course-and-distance on Good last time, would be the main beneficiary if he can reel in a tiring field; Morissette is 116 days off the track and flagged as a fader in finishes, making St Just In Time the more credible threat of the two closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Errors Shuffle Deck
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a loose horse disrupt the race order and gift positions to horses who would otherwise be held up.
scenarios.body: With an inexperienced field of maidens over hurdles, an early blunder by Iwanttobreakfree could see him drop out and allow an opportunist to steal a soft lead; this scenario is unlikely given Skelton's experience but cannot be fully discounted in a maiden hurdle.

watchPoints.text: Iwanttobreakfree sets the entire race shape — if he jumps poorly at the first or second hurdle and loses his pitch, the predictable front-running plan collapses and the race becomes entirely open.

Nightflyer is 77 days off the track and has produced an early pulled-up run (P) in recent form — watch the market to see if Jonjo Jr's confidence in his fitness level is reflected by stable support, as a non-runner or flat display would remove the main threat to the favourite.

Maria Mes has a TS gap concern — her topspeed figure is absent and she has never won over hurdles; if she makes a jumping error at a critical stage she is likely to fade and compromise the prominent-pace picture the scenario relies upon.

Wait At The Gate's unclassified running style means Brendan Powell could place him anywhere from prominent to rear — watch the early stages carefully to see if he tries to dispute for a position, which would change the effective pace dynamic.

With five of the six runners rated OR 120 and all at the same weight (bar small allowances), the race is tightly grouped on official ratings — any minor market drift or support for the outsider St Just In Time would signal yard confidence worth noting in a maiden where unexposed horses can surprise.

races.name: Wotton Printers Newton Abbot Novices' Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Premier Fantasy
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins give this hold-up performer strong claims; Nick Scholfield's string is in fair 14-day form (2/10), Good ground is confirmed fine across all four similar-going runs, and the 39-day break looks manageable for a horse clearly in good heart.
runners_data.comment: Premier Fantasy shaped well when second three starts back and winner four starts back, and his third last time out keeps him in fine heart; experience over today's trip and going suits, and he looks the one to beat off 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Better Off Alone
runners_data.note: A long 165-day absence is a significant flag for Martin Keighley's horse, and its Good-ground record (0W0P in two runs) is thin; it will lead on a small field over 3m2f, but a STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 flags it is operating in an unfamiliar position relative to this race shape, and stamina under match fitness is the key uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Rated 109 and ranked second of five, Better Off Alone shaped with promise when third three starts back, and he carries a hefty 168 lb off a 165-day absence, yet his tendency to pull up — three times in recent starts — is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Knightsbridge
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. takes the ride for the powerful O'Neill yard, and this six-year-old has an outstanding Good-ground record (2W4P from 11 runs) with proven course form at this distance; sitting prominently is his natural role and this race shape plays directly to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Knightsbridge has won two of his last five starts, with back-to-back victories two and three starts back giving him solid recent form, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the main concern is a 42-day absence and a hefty 163 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Lynsey Larue
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose lone Good-ground win came over 24f; trainer Mrs C Williams has no runners in the 14-day window (0/4), and 75 days off is the longest break in this field, so fitness over 3m2f needs monitoring — the form string shows a recent win but also a pulled-up effort.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out after winning two starts back, Lynsey Larue arrives 75 days later carrying 146 lb and ranked last on our figures, making her hard to fancy despite having experience on today's going.

runners_data.name: Flashy Boy
runners_data.note: Fresh from a run just seven days ago and essentially a true rear-of-field type by nature, though shown in midfield here because multiple hold-up horses are competing for the same limited space at the back; Robbie Llewellyn's nine-year-old has been competitive on Good ground before, but a STYLE_FIT discount applies and it faces a tough positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Flashy Boy arrives on the back of a third last time out and a win five starts back, bringing solid recent form into this contest; he has run over today's trip and going, and at 142 lb the weight burden is the one factor he must overcome.

races.paceDynamic: Better Off Alone is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just five runners over 3m2f on Good ground at Newton Abbot, is highly likely to dictate an unchallenged, honest but sustainable gallop from the front. Knightsbridge is the most likely horse to sit prominently in second and keep tabs on the leader, while Premier Fantasy and Lynsey Larue will be deployed further back in their natural hold-up roles. Flashy Boy, a genuine hold-up type, has been remapped to midfield because the field contains more rear-of-field preferences than the race shape can accommodate at the back, but its natural inclination is to come from off the pace. With a single front-runner setting an uncontested tempo over a stamina-testing trip, the race shape strongly favours a prominent racer able to track the pace and strike from a close position at the business end — Knightsbridge, sitting just off the lead, is the profile that benefits most from this controlled, single-pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Knightsbridge Tracks And Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Better Off Alone sets a sustainable pace and Knightsbridge travels prominently throughout before asserting from the last.
scenarios.body: Better Off Alone controls matters at an honest but unforced gallop, allowing Knightsbridge to stalk in second and deploy his proven Good-ground stamina over this trip; Knightsbridge's course-and-distance form (2W4P in 11 Good-ground runs) is ideally suited to this shape and he can strike decisively at the final fence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pair Swallow Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Better Off Alone sets a strong enough pace to come back to the field and Premier Fantasy or Lynsey Larue deliver a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Better Off Alone, returning after 165 days and with modest Good-ground form, runs freely and ties itself up in the final mile, leaving the genuine hold-up horses in Premier Fantasy and Lynsey Larue to pick up the pieces; Premier Fantasy has won twice recently and handles Good ground well, making this a credible alternative shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Better Off Alone Front-To-Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Better Off Alone dictates a genuinely slow pace and kicks clear at the top of the straight, stealing the race from a near-stationery field.
scenarios.body: With only four rivals and no horse willing to chase hard, Better Off Alone coasts in front and produces enough stamina to hold on; its low STYLE_FIT score and long absence temper this outcome, but on a track where front-runners can steal races over staying trips, it cannot be entirely dismissed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Flashy Boy Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and Flashy Boy, remapped from its true hold-up role, gets a clear run to deliver a finishing burst.
scenarios.body: Flashy Boy is a genuine hold-up horse running fresh after just seven days, and if the race is run to suit late closers it has the form to threaten; however, its STYLE_FIT discount and the fact it is not operating from its natural position make this scenario the least probable.

watchPoints.text: Better Off Alone's fitness after 165 days is the critical variable — if it runs freely and burns out in the final mile, the entire race shape shifts dramatically against the leader and towards hold-up horses Premier Fantasy and Lynsey Larue.

Knightsbridge is carrying 163lbs over 3m2f on Good ground; monitor whether Jonjo O'Neill Jr. can hold a smooth position in second without being asked for an effort too soon on this stamina-sapping trip.

Flashy Boy ran just seven days ago and is now being asked to race out of its natural hold-up role — if it is stiff or flat from the quick turnaround, Charlie Price may struggle to place it effectively in a small field where positions are compressed.

With only five runners, any jumping error early in the race could have an outsized effect on the outcome — Better Off Alone jumping well from the front is essential to its chance of controlling tempo, and a mistake at one of Newton Abbot's early fences could immediately compromise its lead.

races.name: Itus Event Support Services Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Run Away Joe
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up performer who has form at this distance on Good going but carries a worrying fade-in-finish flag — at 224 days off the track under a 3lb claimer for Fergal O'Brien (1/10 in the last 14 days), fitness must be queried; his 0W0P record on similar going tells its own story and he needs things to go wrong for the principals.
runners_data.comment: Run Away Joe has run over today's going and our rating just edges him ahead of these rivals, yet he arrives winless in his last five starts and a 224-day absence is the significant concern here.

runners_data.name: Buxted Reel
runners_data.note: The race's lone pace-setter with 12/15 placed runs on Good-comparable going and a recent win on Firm; Tom Lacey's runner was out just 19 days ago so fitness is assured, and with nobody to push him early he can control every fraction — his hold on the race shape makes him the axis around which everything else is calibrated.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but the placed efforts — third last time out and a second two starts back — show he retains ability; the 19-day turnaround is fine and he has run over today's trip and going, though 161 lb is a stiff burden for a horse ranked fifth of seven.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with genuine winning form on Good and a headgear flag (p) suggesting he needs to be switched on; a true hold-up type by nature whose best efforts have come from off the pace, but with so many similar horses in this field he is likely to be pushed closer to the leaders than he would prefer, tempering confidence in him fully executing his pattern.
runners_data.comment: Most Wanted showed smart form when winning three starts back, and a third two starts back underlines his recent consistency; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 160 lb is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Linden Lane
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer for Mrs C Williams under a 7lb claimer, but five runs without a win and a record that consistently shows fifth-place finishes rather than improvement; her natural hold-up style means she too will be pressed into a midfield role she is not optimally suited for, and the amateur allowance only partly offsets the tactical compromise.
runners_data.comment: Linden Lane arrives here 39 days after his last outing in fair trim, and his rating of 91 underlines why he merits respect despite being winless in recent starts; third three starts back hints at capability, and experience over today's trip and going on 158 lb makes him a solid each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Days
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old with a headgear flag (tp) and a recent pulled-up in his form string — his history over longer distances than this with no wins and a patchy jumping record on Good ground makes him a risky proposition, and his hold-up style in a pace-starved race is a further structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Pivotal Days was pulled up last time out and has been winless in his last four starts, making him hard to fancy from stall to finish, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a 36-day break with some freshness possible.

runners_data.name: Ask Peter
runners_data.note: Anthony Honeyball's seven-year-old carries tongue-tie and has a pair of placed efforts to his name, with consistent Good-ground form at similar trips; the trainer is 1/4 in the last 14 days and James Robottom (10lb claimer) reduces the weight, but he is another genuine hold-up performer who will struggle to get a true test of his finishing effort without a stronger pace being set.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Ask Peter faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a second three starts back offers a flicker of hope, though 155 lb does her no favours.

runners_data.name: Estate Planning
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's five-year-old has spent most of his career on Soft ground and steps back to Good — his 5/15 similar-going record underlines that this surface is not his ally; carries a hood and has placed form on Good going, but with 72 days since last run and the deepest hold-up style in the field, he faces the most acute race-shape mismatch of any runner here.
runners_data.comment: Estate Planning has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 91 suggests he holds more than his official mark of 83 implies; the concern is he has been winless in his last five starts and returns after 72 days off carrying 155 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Buxted Reel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge him, Stan Sheppard can dictate terms at a tempo entirely of his choosing over 2m1f on Good ground at Newton Abbot. That uncontested lead sets up a truly galloped, rhythm-controlled race where the pace is unlikely to be punishing early, giving Buxted Reel every opportunity to preserve his stamina reserves for the final climb. The rest of the field is populated almost entirely by hold-up types who will be chasing from off the pace, and with no pressure from behind until the home turn, Buxted Reel can control the race from the front without any meaningful challenge to his rhythm. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or genuine prominent racer who can track Buxted Reel's fractions and produce a sustained effort, rather than a late-closer needing a strong pace to reel in — a slow-to-honest gallop dictated by one horse plays poorly for deep hold-up horses. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Most Wanted, Linden Lane, Ask Peter and Estate Planning are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy, meaning the race shape is even more one-dimensional in favour of the front runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Buxted Reel Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Buxted Reel takes his customary lead, sets a comfortable gallop and faces zero pace pressure throughout.
scenarios.body: Sheppard sets fractions from the front, the hold-up horses behind face an insufficient pace to close the gap in the straight, and Buxted Reel's recent form — including a win and a sequence of placed efforts — proves good enough at this level to last home; his 12/15 record on similar going is a significant asset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting just off Buxted Reel's pace in second or third tracks every move and produces a sharper turn of foot on the run-in.
scenarios.body: With no other front-runner to stretch the pace, the race becomes a tactical crawl that suits a horse who can sit close, conserve energy, and quicken; Most Wanted, with a win and multiple places on Good in this style, is best-placed to produce that effort even if racing slightly out of his preferred deep hold-up role.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field fans wide turning in, creating a gap that allows one of the deeper hold-up horses to produce a late run.
scenarios.body: This is a lower-probability shape because the pace is not expected to be strong enough to bring the closers into the race in normal circumstances, and the redistributed hold-up horses — Most Wanted, Linden Lane, Ask Peter and Estate Planning — face the extra burden of racing out of their natural role; only if something goes wrong for Buxted Reel does this scenario become viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scenario — Buxted Reel Fails
scenarios.trigger: If Buxted Reel makes a jumping error, is pulled up, or fades dramatically, turning this into an unscripted scramble.
scenarios.body: Without the race's only pace anchor, the field loses its shape entirely and the outcome defaults to whoever best handles the tactical vacuum; Run Away Joe's hold-up profile and similar-going record give him the best profile for a messy finish, though his fade-in-finish flag is a concern.

watchPoints.text: Buxted Reel's jumping must be monitored from the first fence — a single mistake at this course could compromise his uncontested lead and fundamentally alter the race shape that every scenario is built around.

Most Wanted, Linden Lane, Ask Peter and Estate Planning are all hold-up horses who will be crowding into a midfield channel together — monitor for interference or traffic problems in the home straight that could block any one of them at a critical moment.

Run Away Joe has been off 224 days and his fade-in-finish flag combined with a 3lb claimer makes him vulnerable late — if he is prominent early and capitulates from the second-last, he could cause interference with hold-up horses attempting to challenge.

Pivotal Days' pulled-up run in recent form combined with the tongue-tie and cheekpieces combination is worth monitoring for any early signs of reluctance or jumping hesitation — a loose horse or refusal at a small field hurdle meeting can cause significant disruption.

Estate Planning's step from Soft to Good ground after 72 days off is a double flag — watch his market move in the final hour for any significant support or drift that signals trainer confidence or concern about his readiness for these conditions.

races.name: Md Elite Cleaning Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Breaking Cover
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist on 39 days' rest for Anthony Honeyball (T14: 1/4), whose sim-going record of 9/15 on Good is decent if not outstanding; the strong pace completely suits this style, though the 168lbs top weight is a notable burden over 2m½f
runners_data.comment: Breaking Cover arrives as the top-rated runner in this field, and his experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead; the concern is that he has finished fourth in each of his last two starts, and his 168 lb burden makes a return to winning ways far from straightforward.

runners_data.name: Centara
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls' OR 127 front-runner has never been out of the first five in fifteen sim-going runs (11/15), but a form string of 1P-645 suggests inconsistency, and sharing lead duties with two rivals of similar style makes dictating on own terms unlikely
runners_data.comment: Centara has experience of today's distance and going, and a win in his recent starts — that victory coming five starts back — though his form since has been patchy, with a pulled up effort in the mix. Carrying 166 lb after 39 days off, he arrives fresh enough to outrun his recent figures.

runners_data.name: Obsessedwithyou
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's seven-year-old boasts a flawless sim-going record of 15/15 and an alternating 1-2 pattern across five recent runs, suggesting high consistency; Gavin Sheehan rides for a trainer firing at 2/4 in the last 14 days, and a prominent but patient style suits this shape well
runners_data.comment: Obsessedwithyou has won twice and finished second three times in her last five starts, a record of dogged consistency, and she has experience of both today's trip and the going; the main concern is 39 days off the track, leaving her fitness to prove.

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Six wins in his last six Good-ground starts make for extraordinary figures (sim-going 12/15, 6W11P), though arriving on just five days' rest raises a freshness or fitness question; Sam Twiston-Davies takes over in the saddle and will need to manage the hold-up position before launching, but the profile is tailor-made for this pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Gore Point has winning form in his last five starts but our figures rank him fifth of six here, and 163 lb is a stiff weight burden to overcome; he does arrive with strong recent momentum and experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies' six-year-old is a confirmed front-runner returning on 58 days off with a trainer strike rate of 0/5 in the last 14 days, which undermines confidence; in a contested lead duel with two rivals it risks burning out before the finish, and form figures of 49-P23 reflect vulnerability when pressed
runners_data.comment: Ice In The Veins has shown consistent placing form, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, and has experience of today's distance and going — our rating of 122 marks him out as a lively threat carrying 152 lb, though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Gower Prince
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill's eight-year-old is a front-runner sporting hood, just 12 days between runs (T14: 2/17), and has winning form on Good at this type of trip; at OR 108 it carries least weight but faces an immediate lead battle with Centara and Ice In The Veins, and at reduced odds of influence its likely role is to soften up rivals for others
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Gower Prince is hard to fancy against stronger company, though he arrives on the back of a win last time out, has run over today's trip and going, and his recent form — a second two starts back and a second three starts back — shows consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Centara, Ice In The Veins, and Gower Prince — will contest the lead from the outset over 2m½f at Newton Abbot on Good ground, making a strong, sustained gallop virtually inevitable. Centara (Paul Nicholls, OR 127) is the highest-rated of the trio and likely to press hardest for the lead, with Ice In The Veins and Gower Prince both needing to be up with the pace to show their best, creating immediate competition for the rail and a genuine test of stamina throughout. This contested pace scenario will stretch the field early, compressing the race for hold-up and prominent types who can travel efficiently before the final circuit. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent horses with proven stamina on Good ground — specifically Gore Point and Breaking Cover — who can exploit the attrition created by front-runners burning each other off.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Centara, Ice In The Veins, and Gower Prince fight for the lead and set a gruelling gallop that drains each other before the last
scenarios.body: The three-way pace battle ensures a strong tempo throughout, leaving front-runners vulnerable in the closing stages as stamina becomes the decisive factor

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Obsessedwithyou travels prominently off the hot pace and produces a fluent round of jumping to pick off the tiring pace-setters
scenarios.body: Obsessedwithyou's outstanding recent form (sim-going 15/15, consistent 1-2 finishes) and prominent style give it every chance to stalk and strike from third or fourth

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Centara Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Centara shakes off Ice In The Veins and Gower Prince early and settles into a controlled front-running rhythm without burning too much fuel
scenarios.body: Paul Nicholls' runner has the highest OR of the front-runners at 127 and decent sim-going figures (11/15), and if able to dictate a measured pace rather than a war, can last home

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Gore Point Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Gore Point — lightly weighted at OR 117 and boasting a remarkable six-from-six winning sequence on Good ground — finds clear air from midfield and produces a decisive late run
scenarios.body: Coming off just five days' rest with a hot trainer angle (Anthony Honeyball T14: 1/4) and a history of routing rivals at this trip, a bold late challenge is entirely feasible

watchPoints.text: Watch Centara, Ice In The Veins, and Gower Prince in the early stages — if all three press hard for the lead, the resulting pace war could produce a dramatically strung-out field by halfway, making hold-up horses' late runs far more potent

Gore Point's turnaround of just five days since last run warrants monitoring at the start; if it appears sluggish or reluctant to settle early, the extraordinary Good-ground form figures may be misleading about its readiness here

Breaking Cover carries 168lbs as top weight, the heaviest burden in the field — over 2m½f on Good ground this is a meaningful stamina concern in the closing stages, even if the pace shape ideally suits its hold-up style

Obsessedwithyou's jumping fluency is central to its chance — if Gavin Sheehan can keep it prominent without becoming embroiled in the front-runner scrap, a clean round of fences converts its excellent recent form into a genuine winning chance

Ice In The Veins has gone 58 days without a run for a trainer with zero wins in the last 14 days — monitor market moves and paddock condition, as a below-par performance here could be an early indicator that it needs this run for fitness rather than arriving at peak readiness

races.name: Compwiz Ltd - It Solutions For Business Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Final Entry
runners_data.note: Lightly framed hold-up performer trained by David Pipe who has strong recent course form, winning over similar good-ground trips; Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim helps at the weights, and the 42-day absence appears benign given Pipe's record with fresh horses — the key question is whether a genuinely slow pace leaves too much to do.
runners_data.comment: Final Entry won two starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a genuine threat at the head of the weights on 168 lb; the 42-day absence is the one factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Jack The Savage
runners_data.note: The confirmed race-shaper here — goes prominently and has won twice at this distance on good ground, with Sean Bowen a major booking; the 53-day break and tongue-tie are minor flags, but 13 of 15 good-ground runs have yielded a finish in the top five, making him the dominant pace influence regardless of the style-fit discount on his mapped position.
runners_data.comment: Jack The Savage won two of his last five starts, including a victory two runs back, and has experience of today's trip and going to draw on; the concern is a 53-day absence carrying 165 lb.

runners_data.name: My Girl Katie
runners_data.note: In scintillating recent form with back-to-back wins, both at this distance on good ground, and Grace Harris's stable is operating at 3/15 over 14 days; the 5-day turnaround is short but clearly deliberate, and racing prominently just off Jack The Savage's pace gives her an ideal position to strike from the second-last.
runners_data.comment: My Girl Katie arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, with the quick five-day turnaround the only query; three wins in her last five starts paint a picture of a mare in sharp form and worth siding with at the weights carrying 162 lb.

runners_data.name: Touchwoodexpress
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies reunites with the family yard and he rides the horse prominently, though recent form figures of 156-76 show inconsistency; the visor is a significant headgear flag suggesting the yard is trying to sharpen his concentration, and the 57-day absence following some poor efforts means there is more uncertainty attached here than the prominent runners ahead of him.
runners_data.comment: Touchwoodexpress boasts experience over today's trip and going, and his win in his last five starts shows he can find the winner's enclosure, with our rating of 91 giving him solid claims; the main risk is 57 days off the track since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Alberts Bay
runners_data.note: Longest absentee in the field at 92 days, which is a real concern for a nine-year-old with a varied form profile; best form has come over shorter distances (18-22f), and stepping up to 3m2½f on good ground for James Best and a small yard with no recent winners is a significant ask — held up naturally but positional redistribution is less of an issue given pace dynamics.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Alberts Bay faces a stiff ask here carrying 153 lb off a 92-day absence, though he has run over today's going before and that third two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Man Oh Man
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who arrives just five days after his last run, but his natural style is to come from the rear and he is pushed forward into a midfield role that does not suit — six turf runs on good ground have brought zero wins, and Bryan Carver will need to manage his position carefully; recent form figures of 59278 offer little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Man Oh Man has been out of sorts of late, finishing eighth last time out and seventh two starts back, and is winless in his last five starts; a rating of 78 ranked sixth of seven makes him hard to fancy, though he has experience of today's going and a second three starts back offers a crumb of hope.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: A four-year-old on a sharp turnaround (four days since last run) for a small trainer, and while placed at shorter distances on good ground, the step to 3m2½f is a very different test for a lightly framed young horse; naturally a hold-up type whose enforced midfield mapping asks him to race out of his comfort zone, and the 0W1P good-ground profile at longer trips does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Blue Siam does at least bring going experience and a placed effort three runs back to the table, but a return just four days ago and a sizeable 145 lb burden make progress hard to envisage here.

races.paceDynamic: Jack The Savage is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a field of seven over 3m2½f on good ground, he is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. My Girl Katie and Touchwoodexpress are both prominent-style runners who will look to track Jack The Savage closely, creating a small lead group that sets an honest but unhurried tempo across Newton Abbot's undulations. Blue Siam and Man Oh Man are natural hold-up types that the race shape pushes into a midfield position they would not naturally occupy, meaning neither is likely to get the deep cover they need to produce their best — their redistribution tags must temper expectations significantly. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a manageable pace with prominent trackers just behind — strongly favours horses racing close to the pace who can sustain their effort over this marathon trip, rewarding the prominent profile above all others.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jack Dictates, Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jack The Savage bowls along in front at a sustainable clip and the prominent trackers My Girl Katie and Touchwoodexpress sit within striking range throughout.
scenarios.body: Jack The Savage sets an uncontested lead, the pace is fair but not punishing, and the race becomes a stamina test for those immediately behind from three out; the prominent profile — particularly My Girl Katie given her recent form — is ideally placed to attack and sustain a run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jack The Savage sets only a pedestrian early gallop and is never meaningfully challenged, saving enough for a decisive kick from the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: A tepid pace suits the horse in front most of all, and Jack The Savage — with his strong record at this trip on good ground and a capable pilot in Sean Bowen — finds a second wind when asked and refuses to be caught.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens sufficiently to string out the field and the prominent runners tire badly in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Final Entry, a hold-up type with strong course form over similar distances on good ground, is best placed of the rear-most runners to pick up the pieces; however, Blue Siam and Man Oh Man are not in their natural role here and their ability to produce a true late run is compromised by their forced midfield positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field suffers significant incidents — falls, unseated riders, or multiple errors at hurdles — that scramble the anticipated race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With a 92-day absence, Alberts Bay is an unknown quantity and could outperform expectations in a messy race; Final Entry's versatility also makes it a beneficiary if the form book is torn up.

watchPoints.text: My Girl Katie arrives on the back of two wins at this exact distance and going — if she secures the position just off Jack The Savage's shoulder, she is the primary threat to any other runner in the field.

Blue Siam and Man Oh Man are both shown in midfield but are genuine hold-up types out of their natural role — if either drifts back to their true position in the early stages, the midfield picture could shift and create gaps for Final Entry or Alberts Bay.

Touchwoodexpress wears a visor for the first time and could either sharpen dramatically or react unpredictably in the early stages — watch how Sam Twiston-Davies manages him from the gate, as erratic jumping could compromise the prominent runners around him.

Jack The Savage's pace is key to the whole race — if Sean Bowen allows him to crawl early, the contest collapses into a sprint from the home turn and the hold-up types gain a marginal foothold despite their positional compromise.

Alberts Bay is 92 days off the track and drops significantly in class (OR 83) — if Jackie Du Plessis has her horse freshened and ready, a bold show here at big odds cannot be dismissed, particularly if the race falls apart late.

races.name: Marilyn And Millie's Retirement Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Quick Sharpener
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 111 and proven on Good ground with three wins in similar conditions, this nine-year-old will press forward from the jump and is ideally positioned to capitalise on Mcgregors Charge's uncontested lead; headgear (hg:t) and 57 days off are minor queries but Gavin Sheehan and Jamie Snowden have a solid 14-day record.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, Quick Sharpener arrives here as the top-rated runner in this field; the 57-day break and a recent unplaced effort are the only notes of caution, but his class — underlined by a rating of 128 — makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Lady Kara
runners_data.note: An outstanding sim-going record of 11/12 on Good makes her the standout form contender in these conditions, and her three recent wins including a chase win at 20f suggest she handles the trip comfortably; Charlie Hammond will be keen to press forward from flag-fall given her prominent style and naturally front-running profile.
runners_data.comment: Lady Kara arrives on the back of three wins in her last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the unseating last time out is the one question connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners a horse in fine form — five wins from recent runs including back-to-back Good-ground victories — but his hold-up style means he needs the prominent trio to fade, which is unlikely given the controlled pace Mcgregors Charge will set; his class (OR 107) ensures he remains a threat if conditions shift.
runners_data.comment: Thickthorn Tom has won two of his last two starts and boasts three wins in his last five, with experience over today's trip and going adding confidence; the main concern is 42 days off since that latest victory.

runners_data.name: It's A Breeze
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls sends out a horse that has won twice on Good ground over 21f and is course-fresh at 39 days, but the hold-up style ridden by a 5lb claimer (Paddy Hanlon) means he needs genuine pace to be set, which this race is unlikely to generate; the 0/0 trainer 14-day stat suggests no particular stable form concern.
runners_data.comment: It's A Breeze has won his last two starts in fine style and arrives here in excellent heart, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the main concern is whether 164 lb tests his resolve under a big weight.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Anchored on OR 81 well below the field on class but holds the critical tactical advantage as the sole front-runner, having run just 12 days ago suggesting fitness is not an issue; his sim-going record (11/15) is acceptable but Ben Godfrey will need to pitch the fractions perfectly to avoid being swallowed up when the prominent pair challenge turning in.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled up among them, Mcgregors Charge is hard to fancy on our figures despite the step up to second last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 12 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Mcgregors Charge is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and will set sail from the front unchallenged, likely dictating at a measured, controlled tempo on Good ground over 2m5f. Quick Sharpener and Lady Kara will press prominently just off the leader, meaning the race will be run at an honest but not brutal gallop with a settled order through the middle stages. The two hold-up horses — Thickthorn Tom and It's A Breeze — will be tracking from the rear, needing the pace to lift in the final circuit to deliver their finishing efforts. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace and strike before the hold-up horses wind up, as a lone front-runner at a sustainable tempo rarely creates enough of a stamina test to fully unlock closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mcgregors Charge sets an uncontested, measured gallop that allows Quick Sharpener and Lady Kara to travel comfortably in his slipstream and pounce turning in.
scenarios.body: Mcgregors Charge controls fractions throughout and the race never becomes a searching test of stamina, allowing the prominent pair to stay on the bridle deep into the race and attack with energy in hand. Lady Kara's excellent form on Good ground (11/12 sim-going record, three wins) and Quick Sharpener's class at OR 111 both suit this shape perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pair Collide Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally stronger than expected and the prominent trio fade entering the final half-mile, leaving space for the closers to deliver.
scenarios.body: Thickthorn Tom, with Harry Skelton aboard and five recent wins on Good ground, has the class and course-appropriate form to sustain a late run if conditions suit a longer gallop. It's A Breeze is less exposed at this trip having won at 21f on Good twice but relies on the pace truly lifting, which is only modestly likely here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies Odds
scenarios.trigger: If Mcgregors Charge is allowed to bowl along at a truly slow pace, never pressured, and simply gallops his rivals into the ground on a flat finish.
scenarios.body: Mcgregors Charge has raced 12 days ago and is fit, and a complete lack of pressure could allow him to steal an unassailable lead entering the final circuit. His OR of 81 makes this a long shot against significantly higher-rated rivals, but a truly uncontested lead over a galloping track is the one scenario that bridges the class gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Tactically
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners jump poorly or incidents disrupt the settled order, scrambling the pace and forcing chaos in the jumping.
scenarios.body: With fences to negotiate and a small field, errors by any of the three prominent types could bunch the field and cause interference that reshuffles expected positions. This chaotic shape is low probability but worth noting given Lady Kara's recent unseated rider (U in form) and the generally tight margins in small-field chases.

watchPoints.text: Lady Kara and Quick Sharpener will both want to press forward behind Mcgregors Charge — watch for either jockey to push for the lead position at the first fence, which could briefly increase the tempo and unsettle the projected settled order.

Thickthorn Tom's hold-up style leaves Harry Skelton entirely dependent on pace being set from the front; if Mcgregors Charge crawls, watch for Skelton to move earlier than ideal and compromise Thickthorn Tom's trademark late run.

Lady Kara has an unseated rider (U) in recent form — watch her jumping at the first two fences for any signs of hesitancy that might cost her the prominent position she needs to exploit this race shape.

Mcgregors Charge's low weight (142lbs) and uncontested lead give him a genuine each-way profile in a small field — watch whether he is allowed to build a lead of more than five lengths at halfway, as that would significantly increase the danger he poses.

It's A Breeze is unexposed over this trip with Paddy Hanlon claiming 5lbs — watch his jumping fluency, as clean, economical jumping in a small field could offset the stylistic disadvantage of being a hold-up horse in a slowly-run race.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Donnie Azoff
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a strong record in similar going (13/15 sim-going score), three wins and eight places from this profile, and a winning mark at 22f suggesting this trip is well within range; Isabelle Ryder takes off a valuable 5lb, and the 46-day break is not a concern given the horse's form without a prep run.
runners_data.comment: Donnie Azoff arrives here in fine fettle, a winner two starts back and runner-up last time out, with proven versatility over today's trip and going; 46 days between runs is the one query, though his quality shines through a rating of 128 and he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: Compelling winning sequence of five from six recent starts with Harry Skelton aboard, and the Skelton stable is firing at a sharp 7/26 in the past 14 days; the two-day turnaround is the one flag to note, but the style-fit score of 0.93 simply reflects that Beorma is being asked to do what it always does — lead — so the discount is minimal in practice.

runners_data.name: King Of The Bronx
runners_data.note: A long 373-day absence is a significant concern for this five-year-old, and the form string features wins only at shorter distances on Good; the finishing fade flag compounds the worry in a race likely to be run at a measured pace where a false position could leave him with too much to do.
runners_data.comment: King Of The Bronx showed what he is capable of when winning last time out, and his experience on today's going is a further asset; the sole concern is whether a 373-day absence has left him short of peak condition.

runners_data.name: Ellerton
runners_data.note: Strong recent form including wins at 17f and 22f on Good ground, with a 45-day break and genuine hold-up profile; the note here is that Ellerton is a true rear-of-field type whose midfield mapping on the pace chart is an artefact of redistribution — in a four-runner field, securing any sort of prominent berth is simply not in this horse's natural repertoire, so Brendan Powell will need a clean late run to feature.
runners_data.comment: Ran a fine second two starts back and scored three starts back, showing he handles today's trip and going; the pull-up last time out is the one thing punters must forgive, though 45 days fresher he arrives with plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Beorma is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only four runners in the field, Harry Skelton will have no trouble lobbing to the front and controlling a thoroughly sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m2½f. With no genuine challenger to press Beorma for the lead, this shapes as a steadily-run race where the early fractions will be modest, placing a premium on class, jumping fluency and a late turn of foot rather than stamina reserves. Donnie Azoff, King Of The Bronx and Ellerton are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the race will essentially be a procession until the tempo lifts coming down the back straight or turning for home. The race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can dictate terms and a hold-up horse with a sharp enough change of gear to pounce late — a slow-run, front-runner's-gift scenario is the dominant probability, with late-finishing types needing a strong sectional in the closing stages to reel Beorma in. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Ellerton, though mapped to midfield due to redistribution, is a genuine hold-up horse and is unlikely to secure any position closer than the tail of this small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beorma Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma dictates a mutualy comfortable gallop throughout, rating an uncontested rail to the line.
scenarios.body: Skelton slots Beorma into a rhythm with zero pressure in a four-runner field, the pace stays honest-but-manageable and Beorma's excellent winning sequence on Good ground makes him hard to pass; the hold-up horses need a late surge that a controlled tempo makes difficult to generate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma's pace is just sufficient to stretch the field and a hold-up horse produces a sharp enough late burst.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up runner finds cover in a small field, tracks Beorma through the final circuit and delivers a late challenge as the tempo lifts in the straight; on Good ground, a horse with confirmed form in these conditions can close the gap quickly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma sets a dawdle and the hold-up horses get into a messy, close-quarters sprint finish over the final two flights.
scenarios.body: A near-crawling gallop bunches the field, stripping away Beorma's rhythm advantage and turning the race into a stamina-neutral sprint that rewards sharp jumpers and tactical awareness; in a four-runner sprint finish, any of the principals can land a blow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Capitulates
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma, racing just two days after its last run, feels the effects of fatigue in the final stages and ties up.
scenarios.body: The two-day turnaround for Beorma is an outlier flag and a horse that has been running consistently could find reserves depleted late on Good ground over an extended 2m2½f trip; any hold-up runner tracking patiently through the race then has only a tiring leader to reel in.

watchPoints.text: Beorma's two-day turnaround is unusually short — watch whether Harry Skelton allows the horse to stride on naturally or whether there is any sign of sluggishness at the start or in the back straight that could signal fatigue.

King Of The Bronx returns from 373 days off and has a recorded tendency to fade in the finish — watch closely over the final two hurdles as any sign of flattening out will confirm the absence has taken its toll.

Ellerton is a genuine hold-up horse in a field of four where gaps may not materialise early — watch whether Brendan Powell finds racing room turning into the straight or whether the small field creates a pocket that kills the run.

With only four runners, the pace scenario is entirely dependent on Beorma's jumping — any mistake or deviation at a hurdle could dramatically alter the race shape and compress the field into a sprint finish that reshuffles the likely outcome.
